title: What Is an Insurance Claim? Step-by-Step Claims Process and Payouts
description: Understand the insurance claims process from start to finish: First Notice of Loss (FNOL), adjuster investigations, repair estimates, deductible subtractions, and payouts.
author: David Sterling

content.text: An insurance claim is a formal, legal request submitted by a [policyholder](/learn/what-is-a-policyholder) to an [insurance carrier](/learn/what-is-an-insurer) requesting financial reimbursement or defense for a covered loss or liability incident.
The 5 Stages of the Claims Lifecycle

items: First Notice of Loss (FNOL): The insured contacts the carrier via app, phone, or portal to report the date, time, location, and nature of the damage.

Assignment of Claims Adjuster: The carrier assigns a licensed adjuster to inspect damage, review police reports, and verify that the cause of loss is not [excluded](/learn/what-is-an-exclusion-in-insurance).
Scope of Loss & Repair Estimation: The adjuster drafts an itemized estimate calculating materials, labor, and depreciation (Actual Cash Value vs Replacement Cost).
Deductible Application: The predetermined [deductible](/learn/what-is-a-deductible) is subtracted from the total settlement figure.
Disbursement & Subrogation: The insurer issues payment to the policyholder or contractor, and then seeks recovery (subrogation) from any at-fault third party.

content.title: Documentation Is Your Greatest Asset
content.text: Following property damage or an auto crash, immediately take timestamped photographs and video of all damaged property before initiating cleanup or discarding ruined items.

rows: Filing for flood damage under a standard home policy
Procure separate flood or earthquake coverage.
Waiting months to report an accident, spoiling evidence
Report all incidents within 24 to 48 hours.
Claiming roof leak caused by 25-year-old rusted flashing
Roommate crashed car without being listed on policy
List all driving household members on auto policy.

items.question: What is a Public Adjuster?
items.answer: A Public Adjuster is an independent licensed claims professional hired by the policyholder (not the insurance company) to advocate and negotiate for a larger settlement in complex property claims, typically charging 10% to 15% of the payout.

content.text: Claims handling regulations and statutory prompt-payment deadlines are enforced by state insurance commissioners.
